subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 new executable Action revisions as one grouped trust update across credentialed automation, security scanning, and release publishing?
rationale: Repository tests can detect many workflow failures, but they cannot decide whether maintainers accept the expanded upstream executable trust set or prefer narrower reviewable batches.

options.title: Approve after exact-head verification
options.body: Review the privileged upstream release changes as a group, rebase the PR, and merge only after the required exact-head checks are clean.

options.title: Split privileged action updates
options.body: Separate Codex Action, app-token, CodeQL, and Docker publishing revisions from routine setup and maintenance actions for narrower trust review.

options.title: Defer the grouped update
options.body: Keep the existing pins and close or pause this bundle until release or security owners have capacity to review the upstream changes.

recommendation.title: Approve after exact-head verification
recommendation.body: Review the privileged upstream release changes as a group, rebase the PR, and merge only after the required exact-head checks are clean.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans the Codex-backed agent workflows and broad GitHub Action runtime modernization, making them the strongest available cross-surface decision owner.
